notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words, and from nothing else: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Where the Quran leaves a person unnamed or names only a title, the draft keeps them unnamed; identifications and later-tradition names appear only in the unknowns and uncertainties. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: The wife of Fir'awn said that he would be a source of comfort to her and to Fir'awn.
She said not to kill him, since perhaps he would benefit them or they might adopt him as a son.
The ayah adds that they did not perceive.

chapters.summary_md: The wife of Fir'awn said that he would be a source of comfort to her and to Fir'awn [c1]. She said not to kill him, since perhaps he would benefit them or they might adopt him as a son [c2].
chapters.body_md: The wife of Fir'awn said that he would be a source of comfort to her and to Fir'awn [c1]. She said not to kill him, since perhaps he would benefit them or they might adopt him as a son [c2]. The ayah adds that they did not perceive [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah does not name the one she speaks of and refers to him only as him [c1]. The words they did not perceive are given after her speech and do not say who is meant [c3].
chapters.kids_md: The wife of Fir'awn said that he would be a comfort to her and to Fir'awn [c1]. She said not to kill him [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that her words hope that he might benefit them or be adopted as a son [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: her name, or whether she believed at the time of these words.
- Not established in this ayah: who she is speaking about; the pronoun refers to the child mentioned in the previous ayah.
- Not established: who they are in the words they did not perceive, or what they did not perceive.

claims.statement_en: God presented the wife of Fir'awn as an example for those who believe, when she said, my Lord, build me a house with You in the Garden, save me from Fir'awn and his deeds, and save me from the wrongdoing people.

chapters.summary_md: God presented the wife of Fir'awn as an example for those who believe [c1]. She asked her Lord to build her a house with Him in the Garden and to save her from Fir'awn and his deeds [c1].
chapters.body_md: God presented the wife of Fir'awn as an example for those who believe, when she said, my Lord, build me a house with You in the Garden, save me from Fir'awn and his deeds, and save me from the wrongdoing people [c1].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah says that God set her forth as an example for those who believe, and it gives her prayer [c1]. It does not say when she prayed [c1].
chapters.kids_md: The wife of Fir'awn asked her Lord to build her a house with Him in the Garden [c1]. She also asked Him to save her from Fir'awn and his deeds [c1].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah presents her prayer as an example for those who believe [c1].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: when she prayed, or what became of her.
- Not established: whether she is the same woman as the one who spoke about the child, beyond the title the wife of Fir'awn.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: she is called Asiya, and later works describe her faith and her end.
Hadith to add later: reports about the wife of Fir'awn, with a named grader for each; none is used here.
